battlecards.why_selected: Matched target pricing in Round 2 and offered the highest total savings and volume-based rebate while maintaining existing service levels and direct-to-patient fulfillment capability.
battlecards.contract_terms: 2-year supply agreement (7/15/2024 – 7/15/2026); firm pricing for term; future increases require market-data justification; volume rebate tier added.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Competitive RFP with six bidders, SKU-level target pricing, and demonstrated ability to switch to Medline/Cardinal created price pressure.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Extensive SKU breadth, existing logistics network with next-day delivery, integrated EDI ordering already in place at all 40+ branches.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Initial pricing above market; rebate structure previously absent.
battlecards.switching_costs: Low—formularies already mapped to alternates; however, staff are accustomed to McKesson’s ordering portal and patient drop-ship process.
battlecards.notes: Choice Health executed contract; implementation completed mid-July with immediate price file update.
complexity_reasons: Contract renegotiation with new rebate structure

battlecards.why_not_selected: Offered only 10 % savings—insufficient versus McKesson’s 20 % and did not match volume-rebate expectations.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Competitive core-list pricing; national distribution footprint.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Could not meet target prices on several top-spend SKUs; limited rebate.
battlecards.notes: Kept as viable backup supplier for future price checks.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Bid issues with unit-of-measure mismatches delayed analysis; projected savings below incumbent’s final offer.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Strong national distribution and acute-care product range.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Data quality concerns during bid (UOM mismatches); rebate proposal not provided.
battlecards.notes: Treya kept Cardinal engaged for future benchmarking but excluded from final award.

battlecards.why_selected: Only viable nationwide lessor with existing 385-vehicle program; agreed to bucketed mileage pricing cutting full-maintenance rates up to 48 %.
battlecards.contract_terms: Service Agreement Addendum (pending signature) implementing new mileage-based maintenance matrix; savings effective retroactive to 6/12/2024 analyses; no change to underlying lease terms.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Detailed utilization analysis revealed only 126 vehicles incurred maintenance monthly; presented ‘should-be’ cost model showing $343 K potential gap.
battlecards.supplier_strengths: Flexible lease structures, nationwide maintenance network, existing telematics integration.
battlecards.supplier_weaknesses: Legacy flat maintenance rate created overcharges; limited transparency on pass-through fees.
battlecards.switching_costs: High—complex unwind of 400+ individual leases; potential early-termination penalties.
battlecards.notes: Addendum expected to finalize Q3 2024; Treya to memorialize terms and monitor monthly savings realisation.

summary.skipped_reason: Categories like Office Supplies and Temp Labor are still in data-collection phase with no final negotiation results; Pharmacy and Telecom on hold or outside current scope.
